paper.title_en: Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory and its application to $X_b$
paper.abstract_en: Following the discovery of the exotic state $X(3872)$ in the charmonium spectrum, the possible existence of an analogous state, $X_b$, in the bottomonium sector has attracted considerable attention of the hadronic physics community. In this work, we lay the ground for the development of Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory (BO$χ$EFT), that allows us to include both quark and hadron degrees of freedom as well as the full complexity of the meson-exchange potential in a systematic way. For illustration, the formalism to leading order (LO) is applied to the system of $χ_{b1}$ states and in particular the $X_b$. The two parameters that are present at this order are constrained using experimental information on the bottomonium spectrum together with lattice input on static quark-antiquark potentials, including string breaking effects. The framework identifies the observed $1^{++}$ state at 10.513 GeV with a predominantly molecular $X_b$, the bottom counterpart of the $X(3872)$, and predicts an additional predominantly compact bottomonium state at 10.544 GeV, about 60 MeV below the $B\bar{B}^*$ threshold.
